cells.location: Tahsildar of Dharmavaram. Findspot
cells.place: Havulūru, Anantapur District. Through Mr. N. Lakshminarayana Rao.
cells.remarks: States that Bhōgi-nāyuḍu, Jikka-nāyuḍu, Jyōti-nāyuḍu and Aṇṇa-Chēmma-nāyuḍu, sons of Mahānyamkāchārya.. Vīra-nāyuḍu, son of Bhōgi-nāyuḍu, Nāgireḍḍi-nāyuḍu and Nārapa-reḍḍi sons of Vībi-reḍḍi, with half share, and Kṛishṇa-reḍḍi and Vēṅkaṭa-reḍḍi, sons of Nūgi-reḍḍi, with the other half share in Dharmavaram, the latter in turn settled several families of various professions such as the potter, the carpenter, the blacksmith, by the gift of the gift village. The tank and the temple of Chēnnakēśava at Dharmavaram are said to have been constructed by Chik-kavodēya of Anegondi.

cells.remarks: Registers a grant of the village Kōtākārā in the Pachchima khanda of the Ramalāya village to Bhaṭṭa Aju[n]ja (or Ajāni), son of Bhaṭṭa Nilakantha and grandson Bhaṭṭa Cheramānja of Kauśika-gōtra and Āpastamba-sūtra. cells.place: TRIPURA
cells.remarks: Records the grant of a village called Ammāśāra together with twenty dronas of land in favour of a Brāhmaṇa family of Mehekala-kula. The grant was originally made by Rāmaṇikya but was ratified by Gōyṇḍamāṇikya and confirmed by Rāmaṇikya in Śaka 1681. This is followed by an endorsement saying that Ratṇamāṇikya re-confirmed the grant in Śaka 1607.

cells.remarks: Issued from Phampāhina-bhukti. cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land, house, etc., made by Mahāprabhu Nidhiyama-gāvunda for the benefit of the Jaina temple constructed by him at Konnur, which belonged to the Jaina shrine at Koldangudla. cells.place: Gold anklet of Śrī-Ranganāthasvāmin (mūla-vigraha).
cells.date: Śaka 1555 (for 1655), Ānanda, Māgha śu. 1, 1=1634 A.D., A.D. January 17, f.d.t. .23. The nakshatra was Uttara-bhādrapada f.d.n. .03.
cells.remarks: Records that the pair of gold anklets with tinkling bells (gej- jēlu) is the offering of Peḍa-Veṅkaṭaperumāḷ-Nāyanivāru, the son of Acyutappa-Nāyanivāru, and the grandson (pautra) of Tūpakula Rāmalin̄gayya-Nāyanivāru. The weight of the set is given as 468 varāha. Below this is engraved a second inscription recording that the anklets were remade with the gold of a damaged anklet of the deity, at the munificence of Jāvira Bāyi Bhāgavamdāsa (Bhagavandāsa), mother of G.B. Narōttam Dās of Bombay, the month of September 1929, and that the weight of the jewel, after remaking, is 183 tolas.

cells.location: Baroda
cells.place: Baroda Museum. Slab in the Museum. From Sadol, Navsari Taluk.
cells.date: A. H. 785, Muharram 24-1383 A.D., March 29; V. S. 1524 (?), Chaitra śu. 13, Tuesday.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Fragmentary and damaged. States that a wall was lying desolate for many years in the village of Sādol(?) and that seventeen persons repaired it, out of their record, and King Firūzshāh prepared it, out of their own money, in order that men and animals of the said village and wayfarers might drink water from it; 16 bighas of land nearby were donated by... (name lost) for its maintenance; Dindha, son of... and Nizām, son of Nașīr, cleared the mud from the date of this deed they were permitted to grow the kharif and rabi crops and sow whatever they liked. The last lines are imprecatory. Also mentions Nizām Attah, son of Maulānā Khwāja. Sanskrit portion, see AI. Ep., No. 51 of 1949-50, App. B.

cells.place: Government Museum. In the Museum.
cells.remarks: States that the Bīghā-i-Jāīdat Bakhsh (the comfort-giving estate) of the Dargāh of Shāh-i-Mīrān, situated at the village of... chand, son of Hans Gopāl, inhabitant of Chakwa Khurd in the pargana of Etāwah, who was the deputy (nāib) of Nawwāb Sa‘ādatallāh Khān, the dīwān and ṣūbadār of Karnātak, came to the pargana of Muslīm in the possession of the local zamīndārs, and had the Dargāh of Shāh-i-Mīrān given a grant of five villages, viz., Kilpāliyāngulī (Kilpuliyanguli) and others, in accordance with the sanad of the said zamīndār, for the maintenance of the god. It ends with the improvement that the writer of the grant or those who shall abide by this order will be guilty of having deserted his dharma and īmān. (cf. Ends with a warning against the continuance of that practice in future.

cells.place: Slab fixed into the Shāhkhān kī Bāolī in Jamlatpura.
cells.date: A.H. 906, Rajab, Wednesday, V.S. 1557, Phālgun-sudi 3=1501 A.D., Feb.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Records that this step-well was constructed by Shivan Kunwar Kāliwānī, a resident of the town of Jatara, during the period of Khān-i-A‘zam and Khān-i-Mu‘zzam Tātār Khān, son of Muhammad Khān. For the Sanskrit portion, see No. 566-A of Appendix B.
